messages:
maria: heads up — I added token-level breakdown panels to per-route dashboards to trace the p95 token spikes across regions.
ashok: which panels exactly?
maria: token.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, token.stage.{kernel_select,batch_queue,kv_fetch}, kvcache.{hit_pct,lat_ms} sliced by route+region. also a small overlay of routing decisions vs cross-region RTT.
kevin: link?
maria: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/token-route-insights?orgId=1
jin: got an alert for /v1/chat/stream — cross-region route failovers jumped ~ 5% at 10:42 UTC
sasha: did we change kernel routing heuristics recently? we rolled kernel-v2 preference for long seqs at 10:30 canary
maria: timeline: 10:30 heuristic canary (10%), 10:35 kvcache compaction on some shards, 10:42 failovers + batching tail
ashok: compaction could explain hit_pct dip -> more remote kv_fetch -> extra RTT
kevin: do we have sampled token traces for affected requests?
maria: yes — click points on the token p95 heatmap to view traces. sample snippet:
```
token 4012: kernel_select 0.25ms, batch_queue 2.2ms, kv_fetch 14.8ms (remote eu-west), gen 0.9ms
token 4013: kernel_select 0.3ms, batch_queue 1.9ms, kv_fetch 0.9ms (local), gen 0.7ms
```
jin: remote kv fetch counts are up; what's causing remote rather than local routing?
sasha: routing rule is prefer-local unless warm_cache_score<0.45 OR kernel_mismatch. compaction likely lowered the warm_cache_score for the prefix.
ashok: also kernel-v2 prepends a namespace to keys in some codepaths — compat mismatch could spike misses until compaction settles
kevin: can we split kvcache.hit_pct by host and canary flag?
maria: did that — canary hosts show ~20% lower hit_pct for the affected prefix between 10:36-10:44
ops-bot: incident opened: #INC-20260325-201 Elevated cross-region failovers — P2
maria: mitigation options: rollback heuristic, temporary sticky-local routing, or proactively warm the kv prefix on canary hosts
jin: prefer sticky-local routing briefly — less blast radius than rollback
sasha: setting routing.force_local=10m for the route now
ashok: I'll kick off a kv pre-warm job for the canary hosts (ETA ~12 min)
kevin: add a small dashboard panel counting routing.decision_reasons (kv_miss,kernel_mismatch,capacity) per route
maria: added a compact table with this query:
```
SELECT count(*) as cnt, decision_reason FROM routing_decisions
WHERE route='/v1/chat/stream' AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY decision_reason
```
kevin: can we show token.latency.p95 split by decision_reason so we can quantify impact?
maria: yes — composite series added. kv_miss path adds ~11-16ms at p95 per token
jin: after routing.force_local flip at 10:55, failover rate fell to 0.7% by 10:59 — mitigation effective
sasha: ops: extend force_local for another 25m while we backfill cache and run a kernel-v2 canary with key compatibility
ashok: pre-warm job finished at 11:08; hit_pct on canary hosts recovered to within 3% of baseline by 11:15
kevin: follow-up actions:
- ashok: pre-warm + verify key namespace compatibility
- sasha: run kernel-v2 canary with compatibility shim
- jin: create alert rule: cross_region_failover_rate > 1% for 5m
- maria: add before/after diff view on token p95 and routing decision overlays
kevin: postmortem note: cascade of kvcache compaction + kernel key namespace change + canary rollout -> cache miss storm -> remote kv stalling -> cross-region tail
maria: will file incident summary and own postmortem once stabilized. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident #INC-20260325-201 status: mitigated (11:20 UTC)
